source.title: Object Detection Using Adaptive Mask RCNN in Optical Remote Sensing Images
source.authors: Amira S. Mahmoud; S. Mohamed; Reda A. El-Khoribi; H. Abdelsalam

record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizers on held-out detection performance, a different task and measure from training-to-test error gaps.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-set AP and recall for several optimizers. It does not measure training error, random-label fitting, or a training-to-test gap. The optimizer comparison bears on V4; the other versions are not tested.
record.test_reason: The study compares optimizers and Adam-to-SGD switching using held-out detection AP, extending V4 to remote-sensing object detection. Training performance and the extent of optimizer tuning are not reported.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's central paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that switching from Adam to SGD improves remote-sensing object detection, and Adam_SGD achieves the highest reported mean AP, 95.0%. Their conclusion also claims computational savings, although Table 1 reports their detector as the slowest comparator.
record.recipe_differences: Compares optimizer variants in a fine-tuned Mask RCNN on one remote-sensing dataset; reports test-set AP rather than training-to-test gaps or matched training performance.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer choice; object category and IoU threshold are also described as affecting recall or precision-recall curves, but no separate numerical rows were extracted for those figure results.

fits_no_version.finding: SGD_Adam reaches 91.2% mean AP, compared with 87.7% for SGD and 90.8% for Adam.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Switching from SGD to Adam can improve held-out remote-sensing detection performance.

record.peer_reviewed: International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol. 13, No. 1, 2020
record.problems: One dataset and one detector family; no reported uncertainty or training-set performance, so the training-to-test gap cannot be calculated. The optimizer comparison does not state a broad hyperparameter-tuning protocol.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 3 and Figure 4 provide optimizer recall/precision-recall comparisons by class and IoU threshold, but precise values are figure-only. Table 1 compares detector methods rather than testing the claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.

Image-classification and language benchmarks; established limited versus broader tuning protocols; training performance; decoupled weight decay. Switching triggers were explored, but tuning breadth and validation procedures are unspecified.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.

missing.what: Table 2's class-level optimizer comparisons reveal heterogeneity hidden by mean AP. Adam underperforms SGD on baseball diamond (96.6 versus 97.1), ground track field (87.7 versus 90.9), harbor (93.8 versus 95.5), and bridge (79.6 versus 95.3), while outperforming it on the other six classes. Class-level comparisons for the remaining optimizers are also unrecorded.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V4. AP measures held-out detection performance, not a training-to-test gap. The split is inconsistently described as 70/30 and as 500 training versus 150 test images. No uncertainty is reported. Class-level results qualify aggregate optimizer rankings.

versions.untested_parts: Network width and test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Language benchmarks, limited-tuning protocol, training performance comparisons, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD as a recovery strategy, and other settings.
Batch size, epoch budgets, and adaptations to large-batch training.
Dropout and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures of the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

rows.note: Test-set performance; training performance is not reported.
rows.check: Numbers are correct: Adam exceeds SGD by 3.1 percentage points of mean AP. Table 2 is on page 74.

rows.subject: adaptive Mask RCNN

rows.note: Reference optimizer for the reported comparison.

rows.operation_detail: Trained with RMSprop; evaluated by mean AP.
rows.note: Test-set performance; training performance is not reported.
rows.check: RMSprop is numerically below SGD by 0.4 percentage points; no uncertainty establishes whether this small difference is reliable.

rows.subject: adaptive Mask RCNN
rows.operation_detail: Trained with A-delta; evaluated by mean AP.
rows.note: Test-set performance; training performance is not reported.
rows.check: Adelta is below SGD by 39.1 percentage points of mean AP.

rows.subject: adaptive Mask RCNN
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD_Adam; evaluated by mean AP.
rows.check: SGD-to-Adam switching does not isolate adaptive versus nonadaptive optimization or test V4's Adam-to-SGD recovery strategy. Its 91.2% mean AP is correctly transcribed.

rows.subject: adaptive Mask RCNN
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam_SGD; evaluated by mean AP.
rows.check: This tests the recovery clause, so reversed is incorrect. Use Adam's 90.8% as the primary baseline: switching to SGD reaches 95.0%, a 4.2-point improvement. It also exceeds SGD's 87.7%.

relationships.condition: Adam versus SGD: aggregate held-out remote-sensing detection AP under the reported fine-tuning recipe
relationships.reason: R1–R2 show Adam at 90.8% versus SGD at 87.7%, reversing the poorer-performance direction in this setting; the limited-tuning condition is unverified.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly achieved 90.8% detection AP versus SGD's 87.7%, but the comparison and restricted tuning premise remain unverified.

relationships.condition: RMSprop and Adelta versus SGD: aggregate held-out detection AP
relationships.reason: R2–R4 report 87.3% for RMSprop and 48.6% for Adelta versus 87.7% for SGD; the RMSprop difference is small and has no reported uncertainty.
relationships.display_finding: Reported average precision favored SGD over RMSprop and Adelta, with a small RMSprop difference and no reported uncertainty; these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Switching from Adam to SGD during detector fine-tuning
relationships.reason: R1 and R6 show mean AP rising from Adam's 90.8% to 95.0% with Adam_SGD, supporting the switching-recovery clause.
relationships.display_finding: Reported mean average precision increased when fine-tuning switched from Adam to SGD, but the comparison remains unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
